research_stage: combination/confirmation of two independently-motivated V3.1 changes, not new signal discovery. Holdout budget: 0 -- paper trading is the forward test.
supersession_note: Preserved for audit. This historical V3.2 proposal included a transition filter whose apparent benefit did not survive controlled methodology. Canonical V3.2 has IBS 0.69, RSI2 0.25, Turnaround Tuesday 0.06, Sector Rotation removed, no Gap Fade, and no transition filter.
prior_claims_verification_note:
The task brief asserts both 'Improvement 1' (remove Sector RS) and 'Improvement 2' (regime transition filter) as 'confirmed' / 'EFFECTIVE' with specific figures. Before writing this preregistration, the repo was checked for computed artifacts supporting each claim, following the same verification practice used in V2/research/preregistrations/v31_transition_filter_v1.json.

(1) Improvement 1 (remove Sector RS) -- CONFIRMED by an existing artifact. V2/reports/v31_regime_decomposition/20260911T002649Z/summary.json's by_regime.sector_rs block shows: FULL-cycle alpha -2.61%/yr (t=-1.09), BULL -2.04%/yr, BEAR -7.65%/yr, SIDEWAYS -4.25%/yr -- negative in every regime, full-cycle figure matching the brief's cited -2.6%/yr almost exactly. This claim is traceable and verified.

(2) Improvement 2 (regime transition filter) -- NOT CONFIRMED; directly CONTRADICTED by an existing artifact. V2/reports/v31_transition_filter/20260911T050458Z/v31_transition_filter_v1.md (hypothesis v31_transition_filter_v1, run the same day as this task) tested this exact mechanism (IBS weight half-sized for 4 weeks after a BULL->BEAR transition) on the live V3.1 spec and found: (a) only 2 BULL->BEAR transitions occur in 2001-2024 under the locked regime-transition definition (2002-04-12, 2011-12-23) -- 8 TRANSITION_ACTIVE weeks out of 1251 (0.64%); (b) neither the COVID 2020 crash nor the 2022 rate-hike bear registers as a BULL->BEAR transition at all, because both pass through one or more intervening SIDEWAYS weeks before reaching BEAR, so the filter's trigger never fires ahead of either episode; (c) measured drawdown reduction for both target episodes was 0.00pp / 0% (not 23% / 20% as this brief asserts); (d) the study's own verdict was MARGINAL (bordering on non-applicable), not EFFECTIVE. The brief's specific '23% COVID reduction' and '20% 2022 reduction' figures are not traceable to this or any other computed artifact in V2/research or V2/reports. A repo-wide grep for '23%' and '20% reduction' found no other transition-filter variant that produced those numbers.

Resolution: per the same rule applied in v31_transition_filter_v1.json (repo's existing precedent: do not silently repeat unverified brief claims as fact, and do not re-derive/re-optimize parameters after seeing a result), this preregistration proceeds as follows -- Improvement 1 is implemented as specified (verified). Improvement 2 is implemented EXACTLY as specified in this brief (same transition definition, same 4-week window, same redistribution idea) so that V3.2 is tested fresh with its own specific weights rather than silently reusing Q6's now-contradicted verdict. However, because the regime/transition calendar is unchanged from the Q6 study (same SPY 200d-MA/252d-return regime rule, reused verbatim, independent of Sector RS), the same 2 transitions (2002-04-12, 2011-12-23) and 8 TRANSITION_ACTIVE weeks are expected to recur, and the same non-engagement against the COVID/2022 episodes is expected. This is reported as found in Phase 2, not assumed here, and not used as grounds to alter the locked rule before running.

changes_from_v3_1.removed_reason: consistent drag in all regimes and all conditional cuts -- wrong frequency for 20-day horizon signal (verified above)
changes_from_v3_1.filter_rule: IBS weight x 0.5 for 4 weeks after first BULL->BEAR regime transition week. Redistributed weight goes to RSI2.
changes_from_v3_1.filter_rule_unverified_premise_flag: The brief's framing of this addition as independently 'EFFECTIVE' is not supported by the one existing computed test of this mechanism (see prior_claims_verification_note). It is tested here anyway, on its own terms, as specified.

ibs.definition: 5-day trailing average IBS, percentile-ranked, earnings-day neutral

signals.weight_sum_note: Normal weights sum to 1.0 (0.69+0.25+0.06). Transition weights as given in the brief sum to 0.81 (0.345+0.405+0.06), an 0.19 (19pp) shortfall from full gross exposure -- larger than the analogous ~6.2pp shortfall noted and left uncorrected in v31_transition_filter_v1.json for V3.1's filter weights. Per that same precedent and this study's own no-reoptimization constraint, the brief's literal weights are used as locked and not re-derived to sum to 1.0; the ~19% reduction in gross exposure during TRANSITION_ACTIVE weeks is treated as part of the tested rule, reported quantitatively, not silently patched.

transition_rule.regime_definition: SPY 200-day MA + 252-day trailing return (same regime calendar as v31_regime_decomposition_v1 / v31_transition_filter_v1, reused verbatim, not recomputed)
transition_rule.restart: if second transition within window, restart 4-week clock
transition_rule.reused_calendar: V2/reports/v31_transition_filter/20260911T050458Z/weekly_AB_nav.csv's transition_active column and transition_calendar.csv are reused verbatim for the trigger timing, since the transition definition and inputs (regime calendar) are identical to this study's. Only the portfolio weights applied on TRANSITION_ACTIVE weeks differ (V3.2 weights vs V3.1's 0.31/0.375/0.162/0.091).

portfolio_construction_method.v31_baseline: Actual persisted score-blended composite_ret from V2/reports/v31_regime_decomposition/20260911T002649Z/weekly_panel.csv, used verbatim -- not a linear-blend reconstruction.
portfolio_construction_method.v32: Linear blend of the already-computed standalone top-quintile signal returns (ibs_ret, rsi2_ret, tue_ret; srs_ret dropped) using V3.2's normal/transition weights. This is the same reasoned-approximation method used for Portfolio B in v31_transition_filter_v1.json, and carries the same limitation: it is not the true score-blended, jointly-selected-holdings portfolio a live V3.2 composite would hold, because V3.2's composite score/ranking is not being rebuilt from scratch (precluded by the 'reuse existing infrastructure, do not recompute signals' constraint). A sanity check (V3.1's own linear-blend reconstruction vs its actual persisted composite_ret, reusing the exact check already performed in v31_transition_filter_v1.json: mean abs diff 0.181pp, max abs diff 2.19pp, corr 0.9975) is reported again here as the best available bound on this method's fidelity.
portfolio_construction_method.limitation: Because V3.1 is measured on its true composite_ret and V3.2 is measured on a linear-blend proxy, part of any CAGR/Sharpe/alpha delta between them reflects this methodological difference, not only the two signal changes. This is disclosed, not hidden, and is a reason to treat a NEEDS REVIEW verdict (if one results) as inconclusive rather than as proof the changes fail live.

adverse_interaction_check.a_calendar_independence: Does removing Sector RS change which weeks the transition filter activates? Answer expected NO -- the regime calendar (SPY 200d-MA/252d-return) does not depend on Sector RS or on any composite weight; this is verified directly by reusing the identical transition_active column computed in v31_transition_filter_v1 (same 2 transitions, same 8 weeks) rather than recomputing it.
adverse_interaction_check.b_sharpe_compounding: Does the Sharpe improvement compound or cancel? Reported from Phase 2 results -- not assumed here.
adverse_interaction_check.c_same_weeks: Do the two changes affect the same weeks disproportionately? Reported from Phase 2 by-regime and episode breakdowns.
